title: Inference
intro: Probability runs from a model to data; inference runs back from data to the model. The two main approaches, frequentist estimation and Bayesian updating, use the same likelihood in different ways.

items: Estimation and Maximum Likelihood (#/probability/inference/estimation-and-mle): estimators, bias, variance, the likelihood, Fisher information and confidence intervals.
Bayesian Inference (#/probability/inference/bayesian-inference): priors, posteriors, conjugate families, credible intervals and prediction.

blocks.text: This is a bridge to statistics, not a statistics course. The aim is to show how the probability on this shelf turns into the methods used to learn from data.

items: G. Casella and R. L. Berger, Statistical Inference, 2nd edition, Duxbury (2002)
A. Gelman, J. B. Carlin, H. S. Stern, D. B. Dunson, A. Vehtari and D. B. Rubin, Bayesian Data Analysis, 3rd edition, CRC Press (2013)
